---
title: "What changed since the parses in synthid"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
options(width = 100)
library(peopleparser)
library(data.table)

# every name of the 10,000-name sample whose parse changed, or that is not
# classified as a person (written by data-raw/compare_versions.R)
d <- fread("../../data-raw/compare-v0.0.9-v0.2.2.csv", colClasses = "character",
           na.strings = NULL)
lg <- grep("_chg$|^any_chg$|^name_chg$|^order_flip$|^split_changed$", names(d), value = TRUE)
for (v in lg) set(d, j = v, value = d[[v]] == "TRUE")
N <- 10000
chg <- d[any_chg == TRUE]
f <- c("salutation", "first_name", "middle_name", "last_name", "suffix")
part <- function(x, w) do.call(paste, c(lapply(f, function(v) x[[paste0(v, "_", w)]]), sep = " | "))
chg[, `:=`(old = part(chg, "old"), new = part(chg, "new"))]
chg[, tok := strsplit(sanitize_input(name), " ")]
chg[, written := mapply(function(t, a, b) {
  pa <- match(a, t); pb <- match(b, t)
  if (is.na(pb)) pb <- match(sub("-.*", "", b), t)
  !is.na(pa) && !is.na(pb) && pa < pb }, tok, first_name_new, last_name_new)]
chg[, middle_split := mapply(function(lo, ln, mn) grepl("-", lo) && !grepl("-", ln) &&
  mn != "" && grepl(mn, lo, fixed = TRUE), last_name_old, last_name_new, middle_name_new)]
chg[, category := fcase(
  !name_chg & !salutation_chg & !suffix_chg, "Gender only",
  order_flip, "First and last name swapped",
  middle_split, "Middle name no longer joined to the surname",
  salutation_new != salutation_old & salutation_new != "", "Title or credential taken out of the name",
  grepl("-", last_name_new) & !grepl("-", last_name_old), "Particle joined to the surname",
  default = "Other changes")]

tab <- function(x, n = 8) knitr::kable(head(x, n))
ex <- function(k, n = 8) tab(chg[category == k & name_type == "person", .(Name = name, `0.0.9` = old, `0.2.2` = new)], n)
cnt <- function(k) sum(chg$category == k)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

synthid's Form 990 Part VII people tables
(`s3://nccs-efile/dev/synthid/partvii-v3_1/people/`) were parsed in October
2026 with peopleparser commit `cb01547`, version 0.0.0.9000, called 0.0.9
here. This page compares those parses with version 0.2.2 on a sample of names,
to show what the changes since then do to real data and where the parser is
still wrong.

## The sample

Twenty thousand rows were drawn at random from each of the 2017 and 2024
people files, and `r fmt(N)` distinct names taken from them. Each name was
parsed again with 0.2.2, with `split_run_together = TRUE` and
`classify = TRUE`, and the salutation, first, middle and last name, suffix
and gender compared with the stored values. The script is
`data-raw/compare_versions.R`; every changed name is listed in
`data-raw/compare-v0.0.9-v0.2.2.csv`. Parts are shown below as
`salutation | first | middle | last | suffix`.

## Summary

`r fmt(nrow(chg))` of the `r fmt(N)` names (`r round(100 * nrow(chg) / N, 1)`%)
parse differently. The rest are unchanged.

```{r}
s <- chg[, .(Names = .N), by = .(Change = category)]
s[, Assessment := c(
  "Gender only" = "Mostly gains: names newly coded from the 2020 census",
  "First and last name swapped" = "Nearly all now keep the written order",
  "Middle name no longer joined to the surname" = "Mostly better; a few names written surname first are now wrong",
  "Title or credential taken out of the name" = "Better",
  "Particle joined to the surname" = "Better",
  "Other changes" = "Mixed; most are compound-surname order and names wrong in both")[Change]]
setorder(s, -Names)
knitr::kable(s)
```

`split_run_together()` changed none of these names: about one Part VII name in
10,000 is written as one run-together word, so a sample this size holds few or
none.

## Gender

```{r}
g <- chg[gender_chg == TRUE]
g[, type := fcase(gender_old == "U", "Unknown to F or M",
                  gender_new == "U", "F or M to unknown",
                  default = "Switched between F and M")]
knitr::kable(g[, .(Names = .N), by = .(Change = type)][order(-Names)])
```

Most gains come from the 2020 census given-name lists, which hold about ten
times as many names as the 1990 lists the old build used. The F/M switches are
unisex names whose balance moved between 1990 and 2020:

```{r}
sw <- g[type == "Switched between F and M", .(Names = .N, F_to_M = sum(gender_new == "M")),
        by = .(`First name` = first_name_new)][order(-Names)]
tab(sw[, .(`First name`, Names, `Now M` = F_to_M, `Now F` = Names - F_to_M)], 10)
```

Gender for these names is close to a coin toss in either census; read the
`gender_confidence` column before relying on it.

## First and last name swapped

`r cnt("First and last name swapped")` names have their first and last names
swapped. In `r sum(chg[category == "First and last name swapped"]$written)` the
new parse keeps the order the name was written in, first name first. The old
build often read a two-word name as surname first when the census leaned that
way at all.

```{r}
ex("First and last name swapped", 6)
```

The others are swapped away from the written order. Some may be right either
way (`Sandoh Mayu`); the rest are the known weakness described under
[Gaps](#gaps-that-persist).

```{r}
tab(chg[category == "First and last name swapped" & !written,
        .(Name = name, `0.0.9` = old, `0.2.2` = new)])
```

## Middle names that are also surnames

The old build joined a middle name to the surname whenever the census listed
it more often as a surname, so `DAVID LEE SMITH` got the surname `LEE-SMITH`.
Version 0.2.2 joins a middle word only when at least 90% of its census
records are surnames (`GARCIA LOPEZ`). Initials are never joined.

```{r}
ex("Middle name no longer joined to the surname", 10)
```

A few names that were written surname first lost a right parse:
`WALPERT LEVY TARA` was `TARA WALPERT-LEVY` and is now first name `LEVY`.

## Titles, credentials and particles

```{r}
ex("Title or credential taken out of the name", 10)
ex("Particle joined to the surname", 5)
```

## Other changes

Most of the rest are compound surnames now kept in written order
(`GUTIERREZ-VALVERDE`), stray words fixed (`KENNETHVAN-DER-VLIET` becomes
`KENNETH VAN-DER-VLIET`) and `DO` and `DOCTOR` read as surnames. About half are
names that are wrong in both versions: an unknown credential left in the
surname (`OWENS-SSND`) or an organisation parsed as a person.

```{r}
ex("Other changes", 12)
```

## Regressions in 0.2.1 that 0.2.2 fixes

The same comparison run with 0.2.1 found names that 0.2.1 parsed worse than
0.0.9. These were fixed in 0.2.2:

```{r}
r <- data.table(Name = c("KATRINA VANDEN HEUVEL", "PATRICIA SAN PEDRO", "ESTELLA DE LOS RIOS",
                         "SIR HUGH TAYLOR", "CHIEF TODD SCHMADERER", "GEN PERRIN",
                         "COL RET CLARENCE MAXWELL", "TOKS MALIK ASHIRU", "DONG JOON YI",
                         "TOBI M E YOUNG", "Albert J A Young ESQ", "BOYD RAY SCOTT",
                         "CHIYA AYDIN AYHAN"),
                `0.2.1` = c(" | KATRINA | VANDEN | HEUVEL | ", " | PATRICIA | SAN | PEDRO | ",
                            " | ESTELLA | DE-LOS | RIOS | ", " | SIR | HUGH | TAYLOR | ",
                            " | CHIEF | TODD | SCHMADERER | ", " | GEN |  | PERRIN | ",
                            " | COL |  |  | ", " | MALIK |  | ASHIRU-TOKS | ",
                            " | JOON | YI | DONG | ", " | TOBI |  | M-E-YOUNG | ",
                            "ESQ | ALBERT |  | J-A-YOUNG | ", " | SCOTT |  | BOYD-RAY | ",
                            " | AYDIN | AYHAN | CHIYA | "))
p <- parse_names(r$Name)
r[, `0.2.2` := do.call(paste, c(lapply(f, function(v) p[[v]]), sep = " | "))]
knitr::kable(r)
```

`CHIYA AYDIN AYHAN` is still read as surname first; see below.

## Name types

```{r}
nt <- d[name_type != "person"]
```

`classify_names()` labels `r nrow(nt)` of the `r fmt(N)` entries
(`r round(100 * nrow(nt) / N, 2)`%) as something other than a person. Nearly
all are right; `Sun Cheer Sheen` is a person labelled an organisation, and
`METTA WORLD PEACE` (the basketball player's legal name) is labelled a person
and an organisation.

```{r}
knitr::kable(nt[order(name_type, -as.numeric(org_score)),
                .(Name = name, Type = name_type, `Org score` = org_score)])
```

## Gaps that persist

* **An unlisted given name before a listed name.** A word missing from the
  census counts as a likely surname, so `DR MASSUMEH FARHAD`,
  `CLEVELAND TAYLER` and `CHIYA AYDIN AYHAN` are read as written surname
  first.
* **Names written surname first with weak evidence.** The written-order rule
  keeps the order unless the census is clear, so `WALPERT LEVY TARA` and
  `Soh Yeun Kim` are read in written order.
* **Credentials the lists do not know** stay in the surname: `SSND`, `SIOR`,
  `CNHA`, `MSCJ`, `FCAP`, `FACFAS`, `CPPO`, `CPSM`, `VG`. Add them with
  `prefixes = c(prx, ...)`.
* **Organisations and notes in person fields** are parsed as people
  (`NORTHWESTERN MUTUAL LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY`, `PHILIP JONES VISIT DALLAS`).
  Use `classify = TRUE` and drop the entries that are not people.
* **Unisex names** (`KERRY`, `TAYLOR`, `KRIS`, `RILEY`) get a gender close to
  a coin toss.
* **Double surnames made of common given names** (`LEE`, `RAY`, `GRANT`) are
  now split into a middle name and a surname.
